text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Conservationists are building artificial nests for golden eagle in remote forest zones so they can breed in peace.
- Ombudsman Lauri Lehtimaja starts own initiative to ensure minority Swedish-language speakers get enough rights to use their mother tongue in legal cases.
- Municipal elections have split Finnish voters in two groups -- rural dwellers voted for opposition parties, but most urban votes went to parties in government. @
- Government to present decision to link the markka to ERM for parliamentary debate on Thursday, but there will be no vote.
- In spite of third-quarter income decline, forestry companies have achieved second-best combined results in monetary terms this year.
- Despite heavy investments, the situation of the forest industry has not improved as expected. Uncertainty about pulp price is so great, some fear it may fall below current $580 per tonne. @
- Finnish shipyards have lost big orders to competitors in Europe and the Far East.
- Unpleasant decisions by government have resulted in negative profile for ruling Social Demcrats, reflected in the party's poor showing in Europarliament and local elections.
- Tampere University hospital to begin research into genetic causes of breast cancer.
- A dog fight in the Tampere suburb of Niemi now needs a court ruling. @
- Media campaigns do not bring change in young poeople's behaviour or attitude to drug use. Most effective to intervene at early school-age, says EU drug specialist.
